questions: For each i, are we to compute the maximum possible GCD among all subsets of size K that include A_i, or the GCD of a specific subset (e.g., the first K elements including A_i)?
If multiple subsets of size K including A_i exist, should we output the maximum GCD over all such subsets, or any GCD (e.g., the GCD of the K largest elements including A_i)?
Is the sequence A zero-indexed or one-indexed? The problem uses i=1,...,N but Python uses 0-indexing.
Can the same element be chosen multiple times? The prompt says 'choose K elements from A', implying without replacement.
Should the output be a single line with N space-separated integers, or N lines each with one integer?
If K > N, is this possible? Constraints say K ≤ N, so not ambiguous.
Are there any time or memory constraints beyond the given limits? The prompt doesn't specify, but typical competitive programming expects efficient solutions.
For each i, if there is no subset of size K including A_i (e.g., if K > N), what to output? But K ≤ N ensures at least one subset.
